runs.market_commentary:
Asia sold off sharply overnight as the AI chip rout intensified. Japan's Nikkei 225 plunged 2.80% to close at 57,002, its worst single-session loss in two months, as Nvidia-linked semiconductor suppliers led declines. Hang Seng fell 1.6% while the ASX 200 edged modestly higher on a Pro Medicus FDA approval. Houthi rebel strikes on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery pushed Brent crude up 2%, adding an oil-price risk premium that partially offset equity weakness in energy names.

Europe opened cautiously with the DAX sliding 1.31% to 25,006, dragged by tech contagion and rising concerns over potential US tariffs on 16 major trading partners. The FTSE 100 held relatively firm at 10,467, down just 0.13%, supported by defensive sectors and the energy bid from Brent's move higher. Germany's Ifo business survey provided mild relief, though ECB speakers remained cautious.

US pre-market futures signal a rough open: S&P 500 futures are down approximately 1.65-1.89% to around 7,084, Nasdaq 100 futures are off 2.86-3.03%, and Dow futures are lower 1.20%. The tech selloff is led by Nvidia (pre-market $147.35 vs. Tuesday close $155.38) and AMD. The critical October PCE inflation print at 8:30am ET — expected near 3.8% YoY — will set the tone for a week already shortened by Thanksgiving. With markets pricing a 97% probability of a December Fed rate hike, any PCE upside surprise risks deepening the selloff.

ideas.catalyst: Sanofi announced a $41 billion acquisition of Insmed, the largest pharmaceutical deal in three years.
ideas.thesis: Acquisition announcements of this size typically trade at or near deal price with limited downside until regulatory review begins. The deal premium is substantial and Sanofi's strategic rationale around Insmed's pipeline supports deal completion.
ideas.key_risk: Regulatory antitrust review or competing bid could delay or reprice the deal.

ideas.catalyst: Nvidia fell over 8% in Tuesday's session and is trading $147.35 pre-market vs. $155.38 close; Nasdaq futures signal -3% open.
ideas.thesis: The AI chip selloff is accelerating on valuation concerns and demand-revision fears heading into PCE data and a possible December Fed rate hike. Technicals confirm a break below key support levels and momentum remains bearish for the holiday-shortened week.
ideas.key_risk: PCE comes in below 3.7% YoY, triggering a Fed pivot narrative and sharp reversal in growth stocks.

ideas.catalyst: FDA granted traditional (full) approval for BridgeBio's therapy for adults and children with LGMD2I/R9 limb-girdle muscular dystrophy; Morgan Stanley raised its price target.
ideas.thesis: Traditional FDA approval removes binary clinical risk and opens the path to full commercial launch with broad label. Morgan Stanley's price target increase signals institutional confidence in peak sales estimates for this rare disease indication.
ideas.key_risk: Commercial ramp slower than expected due to small patient population or reimbursement hurdles.

ideas.catalyst: Houthi rebels struck Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and attacked vessels near the Strait of Hormuz; Brent crude surged 2% and risk premium is building.
ideas.thesis: Ras Tanura is Saudi Arabia's largest oil export terminal and a strike there historically triggers immediate supply-disruption pricing. With Brent already up 2% and ships rerouting, energy equities should outperform the broader market's risk-off move today.
ideas.key_risk: Attacks prove limited in scope/damage; Brent reverses intraday as OPEC+ clarifies spare capacity.

ideas.catalyst: CrowdStrike announced a $43.9 billion acquisition of Zscaler, reshaping the enterprise cybersecurity landscape; analysts upgraded the combined entity on synergy potential.
ideas.thesis: The CrowdStrike-Zscaler combination creates a dominant platform spanning endpoint, identity, and network security, eliminating a major competitor while adding $2B+ in ARR. Analyst upgrades post-announcement suggest the market is pricing in meaningful synergy and cross-sell potential.
ideas.key_risk: Deal execution risk and integration complexity could weigh on near-term margins and slow growth.

ideas.catalyst: Nutanix shares fell ~14% pre-market after Q1 earnings and announcement that CEO Rajiv Ramaswami will step down upon finding a successor.
ideas.thesis: CEO departures combined with an earnings miss create sustained selling pressure as institutional investors reduce exposure pending leadership clarity. The dual negative catalysts suggest the stock is vulnerable to continued distribution over the coming sessions.
ideas.key_risk: New CEO candidate announced quickly and seen as an upgrade; stock gaps back up on relief.

ideas.catalyst: FDA approved EKITNA for advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) in adults who received prior imatinib; shares surged on the news.
ideas.thesis: FDA approval of a targeted therapy in a defined GIST subpopulation validates Cogent's clinical strategy and opens an underserved rare oncology market. The approval removes the primary binary risk and sets up a commercial inflection over the next 2-4 quarters.
ideas.key_risk: Market size smaller than modeled or payer coverage restrictions limit initial uptake.

sources.label: Investing.com: Cogent Biosciences Surges on FDA Approval

ideas.catalyst: Anthropic (Claude AI) is pricing its IPO Wednesday Nov 25 with shares set to begin trading on Nasdaq Thursday under ticker ANT.
ideas.thesis: Anthropic's IPO comes at a time of extreme investor interest in foundation model companies; a first-day pop in a risk-off tape would validate institutional demand. The company's Claude model franchise and enterprise API traction support a premium valuation narrative.
ideas.key_risk: Broader market selloff and risk-off sentiment from PCE data could suppress the first-day open; IPO price set at a discount to recent private round.

ideas.catalyst: Deere reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $3.89 vs. $4.03 consensus (miss) and guided FY2027 net income to $4.50-$5.25B, below prior year.
ideas.thesis: Deere's earnings miss and conservative FY2027 guide confirm that the agricultural equipment supercycle is rolling over as farm income declines and equipment orders slow. The stock's premium valuation relative to cycle-trough earnings suggests further multiple compression.
ideas.key_risk: Commodity prices rebound sharply on geopolitical disruption, improving farmer income and equipment demand outlook.

ideas.catalyst: PepsiCo downgraded citing persistent market share losses to Coca-Cola and private labels.
ideas.thesis: PepsiCo's pricing-driven revenue gains are fading as volume erosion accelerates; private label competition in both snacks and beverages is structurally pressuring margins. The stock's defensive premium looks vulnerable as growth investors rotate away on the downgrade.
ideas.key_risk: Holiday season snack/beverage demand exceeds expectations and reverses market share trend.

runs.market_commentary:
Asian markets surged Tuesday on the back of Monday's historic Wall Street rally, which saw the S&P 500 gain 4.73% and the Nasdaq Composite rise 6.51% — their best single-day performances since April 2025. The catalyst was the unexpected return of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO after a two-week absence, sending NVDA up roughly 31% and igniting a broad-based chip rally. Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 3.91% to 58,644 on Tuesday following a Monday holiday, while Taiwan's market surged nearly 9% on TSMC and related semiconductor gains.

European equities opened mixed-to-higher as the AI-driven rally extended across geographies. Germany's DAX traded near 25,337 (up approximately 2.1% from the prior session), while the FTSE 100 gained 1.3% to 10,480. The dollar pushed to 19-month highs against the euro as Federal Reserve Governor Williams reiterated that inflation remains too high and further rate hikes are possible. The 10-year Treasury yield held near 4.90%, keeping pressure on rate-sensitive equities and growth stocks.

US pre-market is pulling back Tuesday after Monday's extraordinary surge. Nasdaq 100 futures are down 1.73%, S&P 500 futures -0.82%, and Dow futures -0.37%. NVDA is giving back roughly 5% in pre-market after surging 31%, and HPE is under pressure. However, deal flow is active: Sanofi announced a $41bn acquisition of Insmed ($175/share, +46% premium), and the CrowdStrike/Zscaler $44bn deal from Monday is dominating cybersecurity sector news. Earnings are heavy today with Best Buy, HP, Analog Devices, Dollar Tree reporting, and Dell Technologies after the close. PCE inflation data Wednesday is the week's key macro catalyst.

ideas.catalyst: Sanofi announced acquisition of Insmed for $175/share cash (~$41bn), a 46% premium to the unaffected closing price on November 18.
ideas.thesis: Hard-bid all-cash deal from investment-grade acquirer Sanofi with minimal regulatory complexity reduces deal failure risk substantially. At $175 deal price vs current ~$163 trading level, there is approximately 7% spread with a likely H1 2027 close, equating to annualized returns well above risk-free rates.
ideas.key_risk: Regulatory pushback on respiratory drug concentration or a material adverse change clause trigger could derail the transaction.

ideas.catalyst: Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia CEO after a 2-week absence, driving a 31% single-day surge; pre-market pullback of ~5% creates a reentry opportunity.
ideas.thesis: Nvidia's dominant position in AI training chips (H200/B200/Blackwell series) is undiminished by the CEO episode; the fundamental AI capex cycle remains intact with hyperscaler spending commitments extending into 2027. A 5% pre-market dip in the context of a 31% gap-up represents healthy consolidation and a potential long entry for swing traders.
ideas.key_risk: Renewed leadership uncertainty, US export control escalation targeting China chip sales, or a broader AI capex deceleration could pressure the stock significantly.

Yahoo Finance live markets blog Nov 24

ideas.catalyst: CrowdStrike announced an all-stock acquisition of Zscaler valuing the company at approximately $44 billion.
ideas.thesis: All-stock deals trade at wider arb spreads due to acquirer stock risk, but the strategic logic of combining CrowdStrike's EDR with Zscaler's SASE/zero-trust platform is compelling and would create a dominant cybersecurity platform. If CRWD stock holds near current levels, the deal should close, capturing the remaining spread.
ideas.key_risk: CRWD stock decline would reduce deal value; antitrust review in US and EU cybersecurity sectors could add time and uncertainty to the timeline.

sources.label: CrowdStrike and Marvell M&A deals — Longbridge

ideas.catalyst: FDA granted traditional approval to BridgeBio's Welgemda for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9, ahead of the November 27 PDUFA date.
ideas.thesis: Early traditional approval before PDUFA removes binary regulatory risk and signals FDA confidence in efficacy data; rare disease approval with minimal competition in LGMD2I creates durable commercial opportunity. BofA raised price target to $104, Morgan Stanley raised to $95.
ideas.key_risk: Commercial ramp slower than expected due to small patient population and payer access hurdles in rare gene therapy market.

ideas.catalyst: Dick's Sporting Goods rose more than 16% after reporting stronger-than-expected Q3 results, beating both EPS and revenue estimates.
ideas.thesis: A 16%+ earnings gap often leads to continued momentum as funds that missed the initial move buy in on the first pullback; the print signals consumer spending resilience in discretionary athletic goods. Strong same-store sales growth supports multiple expansion at current levels.
ideas.key_risk: Post-earnings fade as short-term momentum exhausts itself, and macro headwinds from a potential 10-year at 4.9%+ weigh on consumer discretionary valuations.

sources.label: Yahoo Finance stock market news Nov 24

ideas.catalyst: Dollar Tree jumped ~9% pre-market after reporting results that beat revenue expectations, driven by value-seeking consumer behavior.
ideas.thesis: With the 10-year yield near 4.9% and consumer confidence under pressure, households are trading down to discount retailers — a structural tailwind for Dollar Tree. A 9% gap on results with potential for follow-through momentum makes this an attractive short-term long.
ideas.key_risk: Analyst downgrades post-earnings, rising import costs from tariff uncertainty, or broad consumer retail sector rotation could limit upside.

ideas.catalyst: Marvell announced an all-stock acquisition of Lumentum valued at approximately $115 billion, expanding its photonics and optical interconnect capabilities for AI data centers.
ideas.thesis: Lumentum's optical components are critical for high-bandwidth AI cluster interconnects; the deal positions Marvell as a full-stack AI silicon supplier competing against Broadcom. The deal demonstrates executive confidence in AI data center spending durability and could attract a multiple re-rating.
ideas.key_risk: Integration complexity, all-stock dilution, and potential antitrust review of combined optical-silicon market share could weigh on shares near-term.

sources.label: CrowdStrike and Marvell M&A deals — Longbridge

ideas.catalyst: Taiwan's market surged nearly 9% on NVDA CEO reinstatement news; TSMC is the primary manufacturer for Nvidia's Blackwell GPU generation.
ideas.thesis: TSMC's leading N3/N2 process nodes have no credible near-term alternative for Nvidia's next-gen chips; AI capex super-cycle continues driving wafer demand well above consensus. TSM ADR trades at a discount to intrinsic value given a geopolitical risk premium that appears mispriced in a benign scenario.
ideas.key_risk: Taiwan Strait tensions, US export controls tightening further, or a sudden AI capex pause by hyperscalers would severely pressure the stock.

sources.label: Nasdaq/Dow/S&P futures Nvidia rally — Yahoo Finance
CaixaBank financial markets daily report Nov 24

ideas.catalyst: Fed Governor Williams stated inflation remains too high and that further rate hikes are possible, with 10-year yield near 4.90%.
ideas.thesis: With the Fed signaling a hawkish stance and PCE data due Wednesday, long-duration bonds face asymmetric downside risk. TLT moves inversely to yields; a PCE print above consensus could drive the 10-year toward 5.0%+, compressing TLT by 2-4%.
ideas.key_risk: A softer-than-expected PCE print or a risk-off episode driving a flight to safety would cause TLT to rally sharply, hurting the short position.

sources.label: The CIO Brief Nov 24 — Williams rate hike commentary

ideas.catalyst: Arista Networks was upgraded by analysts citing accelerating AI hyperscaler data center build-outs driving sustained demand for high-speed Ethernet switching.
ideas.thesis: Arista is the primary beneficiary of hyperscaler AI network upgrades, with 400G/800G Ethernet displacing InfiniBand in many workloads; the company consistently beats estimates and guides conservatively. The AI infrastructure super-cycle makes Arista's revenue visibility unusually high for a growth stock.
ideas.key_risk: Competition from Cisco's Nexus portfolio, a slowdown in hyperscaler capex, or a macro-driven IT spending cut could reduce growth rates and compress the multiple.

deals.headline: Sanofi Acquires Insmed for $41 Billion in Largest Pharma Deal in Three Years
deals.description: Sanofi agreed to acquire Insmed at $175 per share in an all-cash deal valuing the respiratory disease company at approximately $41 billion, a 46% premium to the unaffected closing price on November 18, 2026. The deal centers on Insmed's BRINSUPRI (brensocatib) and ARIKAYCE platforms for non-tuberculosis mycobacterial lung disease and other serious respiratory indications.
deals.impact: High — Insmed surged 14%+ on the news; deal expected to close H1 2027

deals.headline: CrowdStrike to Acquire Zscaler in $44 Billion All-Stock Cybersecurity Merger
deals.description: CrowdStrike announced a definitive agreement to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock transaction valuing Zscaler at approximately $44 billion, creating the largest pure-play cybersecurity company globally. The combined entity would offer an end-to-end security platform combining CrowdStrike's Falcon endpoint detection with Zscaler's zero-trust network access and SASE capabilities.
deals.impact: High — Transformative deal reshaping the cybersecurity sector landscape
deals.sentiment: Bullish for ZS; mixed for CRWD (dilution risk)

deals.headline: Marvell Technology Acquires Lumentum in $115 Billion All-Stock Deal for AI Photonics
deals.description: Marvell Technology announced an all-stock acquisition of optical components maker Lumentum, valued at approximately $115 billion, to build out photonic interconnect capabilities for AI data center infrastructure at scale. The deal positions Marvell as one of the largest AI silicon suppliers with end-to-end data center networking solutions from chip to optical transceiver.
deals.impact: Very High — Creates a major AI silicon-to-photonics platform company
deals.sentiment: Bullish for LITE; watch for MRVL dilution near-term

deals.headline: Eli Lilly Agrees to Acquire Calytrix Bio for Up to $1.5 Billion
deals.description: Eli Lilly announced a deal to acquire Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5 billion, adding an early-stage pipeline candidate in metabolic disease to its already-robust GLP-1 and metabolic franchise. The deal includes an upfront payment with milestone-based earnouts, consistent with Lilly's strategy of bolt-on acquisitions to supplement organic R&D.
deals.impact: Low-Medium — Incremental pipeline addition; minimal near-term earnings impact

deals.headline: Johnson & Johnson Acquires Ollin Biosciences for $2.2 Billion Upfront
deals.description: Johnson & Johnson announced an agreement to acquire Ollin Biosciences for $2.2 billion upfront, adding a next-generation immunology pipeline to complement its MedTech and pharmaceutical portfolio. The deal continues J&J's pattern of building out its immunology franchise through targeted bolt-on acquisitions post the Kenvue spinoff.
deals.impact: Low-Medium — Pipeline accretion in immunology; credit-positive for Ollin
